findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_threat_indicators, get_cve_details, get_ioc_context, get_ioc_batch, check_wallet_sanctions, check_domain_age · Private data: get_threat_indicators, get_ioc_context, check_wallet_sanctions · Public sink: subscribe_alerts, submit_indicator · Destructive: check_wallet_sanctions.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_threat_indicators, get_cve_details, get_ioc_context, get_ioc_batch, check_wallet_sanctions, check_domain_age · Private data: get_threat_indicators, get_ioc_context, check_wallet_sanctions · Public sink: subscribe_alerts, submit_indicator · Destructive: check_wallet_sanctions

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_threat_indicators" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
